question: When professional tennis players challenge a line call with Hawk-Eye, roughly how often are they proved right?
answer: About two times in five. Mather examined about 1,500 challenges from 2006 and 2007: nearly all involved balls within 10 cm of the line, and the line judges were upheld about 60% of the time. Players challenged because they felt sure they had seen it, and they were wrong more often than right.
move: Feeling sure is not evidence, least of all on close calls.
ask: On a close call this week, how sure am I really, and what would I bet on it?
trap: Assuming players challenge only when they clearly saw it out.
source: Mather, Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2008
reference: George Mather, Perceptual uncertainty and line-call challenges in professional tennis, Proceedings of the Royal Society B, 2008
